results.title: Reach Consensus Faster by Using IAA Charts in the Annotation Lab - John Snow Labs
results.content: # Reach Consensus Faster by Using IAA Charts in the Annotation Lab. Lead of John Snow Labs Medical Annotators Team. Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA) is a measure of how consistent or aligned the manual annotations created by different team members are. ## User-friendly Inter-Annotator Agreement Charts. The first chart on the IAA page gives a general overview of the level of agreement between the two annotators selected from the right-side dropdowns. ##### Percentage pie-chart of High-Level IAA chart (Annotation Lab 3.5.0). The percentage of inter-annotator agreement for each label in the taxonomy is displayed in a user-friendly style in the following chart. Apart from identifying challenging labels (which would require AG refinement), using this chart you can spot single annotators that may not be following the most updated extraction rules. ##### Inter Annotator Agreement chart on all common tasks (Annotation Lab 3.5.0). The following chart provides a very specific chunk level agreement test between two annotators. All chunks included in their common tasks will be compared and whenever the label used by the two annotators do not match, a disagreement will be flagged. This analytics chart compares predictions and ground truth annotations and can be generated for each annotator-model pair. Another helpful chart is the **Chunk Extracted by Annotator**. ##### Chunks extracted by annotator (Annotation Lab 3.4.0). As such, in the **Chunks Extracted by Label** chart, users can see how often an individual chunk was annotated with a particular Label by each one of the annotators assigned to the project. ##### Chunks extracted by label (Annotation Lab 3.4.0). In this series of 3 blog posts, I illustrated the usage and utility of each one of the analytical charts provided out-of-the-box by the Annotation Lab. By default, the Analytics dashboards page is disabled. Changes made by the annotators (like creating tasks, adding new completion, etc.) will not be automatically reflected in the Analytics charts.
